title: PRD: translate incident action items into scorable deployment resilience requirements
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: convert prioritized postmortem action items from the KV-cache + autoscale incident into a single PRD appendix that defines scorable, testable deployment resilience requirements. The appendix will be used by eng and SRE to implement runtime changes, by Console/DevExp to add operator checks, and by QA to craft synthetic verification. Deliverables: (1) table of requirements mapped to incident action items, owner, acceptance criteria and automated verification; (2) updated rollout gating and canary checks in the PRD; (3) operator checklist and synthetic test harness definitions; (4) telemetry and dashboard success metrics. This ticket covers authoring the PRD text, circulating for cross-functional review, and encoding the acceptance criteria into testable items for the release verification pipeline.
context: Root incident: kv-cache stall + coldstart autoscale overload (postmortem link below) produced a 3-hour degradation affecting hosted API tail latency and customer error rates. The postmortem contains 12 action items across runtime, autoscaler policies, and monitoring. SRE prioritized five action items as high-severity due to customer impact and recurrence risk. Engineering requested clarifications on the required rollout constraints and rollback gates. Product must convert these operational actions into explicit PRD requirements so implementation teams have deterministic acceptance criteria and operators have clear go/no-go checks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Every high-priority postmortem action must be represented as a requirement row with: ID, one-line requirement, owner, SLO target or threshold, verification step, and rollback criterion.
A2: Requirements must be scorable: each row receives a PASS/FAIL/NA outcome and a confidence score used by release automation to block canaries if any FAILs are observed.
A3: Synthetic verification harness definitions for each requirement are added (payloads, load patterns, expected metrics), and one automated test per requirement is included in the release pipeline.
A4: Operator runbook section updated with a 6-step troubleshooting checklist, severity triage matrix, and clear escalation path to SRE on-call (names/roles to be templated).
A5: Dashboard and alert specifications updated: metric names, aggregation windows, alert thresholds, and a post-deployment verification dashboard (template link included).
A6: Cross-functional review completed and signoffs captured from SRE lead, Runtime Eng PM, and Console owner.

A7: Release gating rules encoded: at least 90% of scorable requirements PASS in the canary region for 30 minutes before full rollout; a single FAIL in a P0 requirement should automatically trigger rollback or manual approval with justification recorded.
A8: PRD appendix published and linked from the runtime-1.20 release notes and the deployment checklist repository.
scope_changes: Included: mapping of only the five SRE-prioritized high-severity action items into scorable requirements; creation of synthetic tests for those five items.
Excluded: lower-priority postmortem items and architectural redesign proposals — these will be tracked in separate PM tickets after initial hardening is complete.
Decision log: agreed 2026-03-11 with SRE to phase remaining items into Q2 scope to avoid blocking runtime-1.20 launch.
proposed_solution: Author a PRD appendix (scorable requirement table) + operator runbook + synthetic test definitions. For each requirement: derive numeric pass thresholds from historical telemetry where possible (e.g., tail P99 latency increase < 30ms under 95th percentile load) or specify deterministic functional checks (e.g., cache regen completes within Xs without request queuing). Add automation hooks so the release pipeline can query PASS/FAIL state and confidence score. Implement gating: automatic hold if any P0 requirement FAILs, otherwise require explicit product/SRE approval with recorded rationale.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting thresholds to today's telemetry may cause false positives during benign traffic shifts. Mitigation: use rolling-week baselines and require a confidence interval in the scorable calculation.

Risk: Teams may implement only the checkbox but not the underlying root cause fix. Mitigation: require an owner and an implementation plan linked to each requirement; track completion stories in the runtime epic.

Risk: Synthetic tests add CI runtime and flakiness. Mitigation: keep most tests in a dedicated release-verification pipeline and mark long/fragile checks as optional for developer PRs but required for canary gating.
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Draft mapping completed — 5 high-priority action items reduced to 8 scorable requirement rows. Reviewed with SRE (Jonas Weber) and Runtime Eng lead (Maya Chen). Clarified that rollback must include automatic model variant fallback plus capacity reduction path.

2026-03-12: Added synthetic harness templates and annotated which metrics will be used. Engineering asked for example payloads; linked sample payloads in artifacts. Assigned owners for each requirement.
2026-03-13: Design/Console sync — operator checklist mockups created; Console owner requested an extra 'false positive' confirmation step for alerts. Incorporated request.
2026-03-14: Sent PRD appendix to cross-functional reviewers. Pending signoffs from SRE lead and Console owner. Identified one dependency on autoscaler policy rewrite (ENG-4021).
QA_plan: Create per-requirement synthetic tests: low-load functional checks + stress scenarios replicating the incident pattern.
Run canary in 2 regions for 60 minutes with telemetry aggregation; automated PASS/FAIL evaluation reported to release dashboard.
Post-deploy 24h regression monitoring with auto-created ticket if any P0 metrics deviate beyond threshold.
